ramp-test.short: A graded exercise test where power rises smoothly, e.g. 25 W every minute added in small steps every few seconds, from easy to exhaustion.

step-test.short: A graded exercise test with longer stages (often 3–5 min), each held at one power or pace before the next rise, so blood lactate and heart rate can settle.

peak-power-output.short: The highest power reached at the end of a ramp or step test, sometimes called maximal aerobic power. It depends on the protocol, not only on the athlete.

douglas-bag.short: The classic way to collect breath: all the air breathed out over a set time goes into a large bag, then its volume and O₂ and CO₂ are measured. Slow, but the reference for checking other systems.

mixing-chamber.short: A small box in a metabolic cart where several breaths mix before the gas is sampled. It gives smooth readings but can't follow fast changes.

breath-by-breath.short: Gas measurement where a flow sensor and fast gas analysers work out VO₂ and CO₂ output for every single breath. Detailed, but noisy from breath to breath.

calibration.short: Checking and adjusting a device against a known standard before use, e.g. a gas of known O₂ and CO₂ content, or a 3 L syringe of air pumped through a flow sensor.

averaging-interval.short: The time (or number of breaths) over which raw gas data are averaged before the peak is read, e.g. 15 s or 30 s. A shorter interval gives a higher, noisier peak.

validity.short: Whether a test or device measures what it claims to: its results agree with a reference measure. A device can repeat itself well and still be wrong.

three-minute-all-out-test.short: A 3-minute effort flat out from the first second, with no pacing. Power falls, then levels off; the power over the last 30 s is used to estimate critical power.

end-test-power.short: The mean power over the last 30 s of a 3-min all-out test, used as an estimate of critical power.

w-prime.short: The fixed amount of work, in kJ, that you can do above critical power before you must slow down. Hard efforts above CP use it up; riding below CP slowly refills it.

cooper-test.short: A running field test: cover as much distance as you can in 12 minutes. The distance is used to estimate VO2max.

yo-yo-test.short: A shuttle test: 2 × 20 m runs at speeds set by beeps that keep rising, with 10 s of easy jogging between. The distance covered before you can't keep up measures repeated hard-running ability.

zero-offset.short: What a power meter reads with no force on the pedals. Resetting it ('zeroing') before a ride stops temperature changes from shifting every reading.

icc.short: A retest correlation from 0 to 1: how well a group keeps its order when everyone repeats a test. A high ICC can come with a typical error too big for tracking one athlete.
